correctness.rationale: For m=n−1 and r=q−1 the exact overlap graph is balanced with degrees r, q, and 1 on weights 0,1,2. Zero appends lead to the root from every vertex, hence by balance every nonisolated vertex belongs to one strongly connected component. Each rotation class has a unique Euler edge sequence beginning at the labelled edge 0^m1, so the fixed-first-edge BEST count has no extra division. Each weight-two vertex's outgoing choice is forced and its zero path reaches a one-color vertex. On deleting the root row and column, elimination along these paths preserves the tree count: one-color index i can shift forward with its color unchanged or reflect to m−1−i in any of r colors. The operator on zero-sum colors is a triangular shift with diagonal q in each of q−2 directions; the constant-color block is the reflected index tree operator with weights 1 and r. Any reflected choice at i≥floor(m/2) traps the closed interval [m−1−i,i]; all assignments reflecting only at lower indices strictly progress to the root. Thus the remaining determinant is q^floor(m/2). This includes m=1, where colored self-loops must be subtracted and the index block determinant is 1. Combining the determinant and BEST gives the stated product. The number of distinct windows is n(q−1)+C(n,2)(q−1)² and a shorter period would repeat a window. Fresh depth-first enumeration by unused labelled windows independently matches 12, 432, 5184, 6912 at the four stated pairs; finite checks supplement the proof.
residual_risks: Rotation only; labels and loops matter. Adding 0^n or quotienting symbols changes the counting problem.
